data.title: The Friendship Recession: The lost art of connecting
data.author: 47thpresident
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了美国社会正经历的“友谊衰退”现象，即人们越来越少拥有亲密朋友。自1990年以来，没有亲近朋友的美国成年人比例增加至12%，而拥有十个以上亲密朋友的人数减少了近三倍。造成这一现象的原因包括郊区扩张导致人们物理距离增加，政府对社区中心等“第三空间”的投资减少，以及零工经济和经济压力使得闲暇时间成为奢侈。尽管结构性因素是主因，文化转变也不可忽视。工作成为主要社交身份，许多人优先考虑职业而非个人关系。此外，过度关注核心家庭的“密集育儿”方式也挤压了成年人之间的社交时间。文章警告，如果不重新调整优先事项和学习培养有意义的关系，人们可能会失去建立和维持友谊的能力，进而影响幸福感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：现代社会中友谊的形成与维持面临的挑战及其原因

不同观点：
• [dm03514] 认为现代社会的个体主义导致了人们与社区的互动减少，互联网和便捷的服务让人们无需面对面交流，从而加剧了友谊的衰退。个人优先考虑自己而非社区，形成了“晚期个体主义”。
• [prhn] 提出现代社会对友谊的期望不切实际，受到影视作品影响，人们期望朋友像“无条件支持的治疗师”，而实际上友谊形式多样，且大多数友谊是阶段性的。现代人缺乏主动参与社区活动的动力，因为这需要勇气和持续的努力。
• [zkmon] 认为国家概念削弱了社区和友谊的需求，现代社会鼓励个体成为无连接的工人，从而削弱了内部结构和自主团体。
• [oddthink] 质疑人们是否有足够时间投入友谊，尤其是有孩子的家庭，每天的时间被工作和家庭责任填满，难以抽出时间社交。
• [dazzawazza] 强调面对面互动和共享实体物品（如专辑、书籍）能够增强信任和友谊，批评数字世界的贫困化导致友谊质量下降。
• [MattGaiser] 认为友谊衰退的主要原因是需求下降，而非社交空间供应不足，因为现有的社区中心和公共场所利用率不高。
• [NalNezumi] 指出人们对友谊的期望提高，现代社会对新连接的功利性期望增加，导致交友变得更加困难。
• [subpixel] 强调友谊的质量重于数量，真正的友谊需要时间和经历去培养，且这些友谊不易形成，特别是在中年阶段。
• [baazaa] 认为社交被视为一种负担，许多人实际上并不享受社交活动，这可能是社交减少的简单解释。
• [rorylaitila] 指出大多数人缺乏主动社交的执行力，尽管享受与朋友的相处时光，但很少有人主动去维持友谊。
• [gitroom] 认为现代社会交友变得困难，许多人因此放弃尝试，但看到别人成功建立友谊是一种鼓舞。
• [mindwok] 认为西方国家普遍存在友谊减少、弱化的趋势，这是现代社会面临的最大挑战之一，尽管技术进步，但人们仍然感到孤独和孤立。
• [peakskill] 反驳那些认为有家庭无法社交的观点，指出欧洲的第三空间允许孩子与父母一起社交，并认为更多的第三空间能提高社会信任度和独立性。

补充讨论：
• 友谊的形式和期望在现代社会中发生了变化，许多人对友谊的定义和需求不再一致。
• 互联网和数字技术在提供便利的同时，也减少了面对面社交的机会和必要性。
• 社区中心和公共场所的使用率下降反映了现代社会对主动社交活动的需求减弱。
• 有观点认为国家和社会结构在鼓励个体独立的同时，削弱了社区和友谊的重要性。
• 时间管理和家庭责任被认为是影响人们社交能力的重要因素。

争议焦点：
• 友谊衰退的原因是供需问题还是社会结构性变化。
• 现代社会对友谊的期望是否过高，导致交友困难。
• 互联网和数字技术对社交的影响是积极还是消极。

43802727.article_content:
The Friendship Recession: The Lost Art of Connecting
Feb 28
Written By
Bryce Fuemmeler
February 2025 Issue
Carolyn Bruckmann, Harvard Kennedy School MPP ‘25
The so-called “Friendship Recession” is making its way into the vernacular—a profound shift in how Americans experience and sustain friendships. The data paints a stark picture. According to the
American Perspectives Survey
, the percentage of U.S. adults who report having no close friends has quadrupled to 12% since 1990, while the percentage of those with ten or more close friends has fallen by nearly threefold. The foundations of the crisis were laid long before lockdowns. For decades, Americans consistently spent about 6.5 hours a week with friends. Then, between 2014 and 2019, that number plummeted to just four hours per week.
To be sure, systemic forces underlie this shift.
Suburban sprawl
has physically distanced us from one another.
The government slowed down
its investment in and construction of
third spaces
—such as community centers, parks, and coffee shops—which has left fewer places for organic social interactions. The rise of the
gig economy
and economic pressures have made free time a luxury. These factors have made friendship more difficult, and policymakers, urban planners, and venture capitalists are searching for solutions.
However, these structural forces alone can't fully account for the larger shift. If inaccessibility were the primary driver, we wouldn’t see relatively
stable connection rates
among older adults over the last several decades. If wealthier individuals have more access to communal spaces, why has
solo dining increased by 29% in the past two years
? If this were purely circumstantial, why would Stanford now offer
Design for Healthy Friendships
—a class dedicated to helping students structure their social lives with intention?
These trends point to something more insidious: a cultural crisis. As
Anne Helen Petersen writes
, “time for friends is a privilege, but it is also a matter of priorities.” The way we spend our time, whom we invest in, and what we prioritize is shifting.
Solitude is becoming more than a preference
—it’s becoming a default. And when not used
well
, the result of solitude isn’t just fewer friendships—it’s a fundamental loss of the ability to form and sustain them. If we don’t consciously reshape our priorities and re-learn how to cultivate meaningful relationships, we risk a future where connection—one of the most fundamental sources of happiness and well-being—fades into the background of our lives.
The cultural shift
Work has become a dominant social identity
It’s often said that if you ask an American what they do, they’ll tell you about their job, whereas a European might talk about their hobbies or passions. Data backs this up; U.S. workers put in an average of
1,799 hours per year
, which is 182 more hours than the OECD country average. But the role of work in shaping identity and social life in the United States has perhaps never been stronger. For example,
77% of Americans
work more than 40 hours per week, and
few take their full paid leave
.
Pew Research
suggests that the percentage of adults 65 and older who are employed has nearly doubled since 1987, rising from 11% to 19%.
These shifts are in part driven by broader
economic forces
. Higher cost of living and stagnating wages for low-and middle-income earners means that everyday Americans must work harder to keep up. However, these shifts also suggest a deeper cultural transformation may be occurring—one where the old American ethos of working hard and climbing the economic ladder has evolved into an all-consuming, identity-defining pursuit that leaves little room for much else.
In a study
of generational shifts in work values in the United States, researchers found that Americans are placing greater importance on intrinsic work values—such as having interesting jobs and work that helps others and society. Finding meaning in work (obviously) isn’t a problem
per se.
Yet when finding fulfillment in work comes at the expense of meaningful personal relationships, it becomes a problem—one that risks leaving individuals fulfilled in their careers but isolated in their personal lives.
The focus is increasingly on the nuclear family
As work has become increasingly all-encompassing, Americans have also doubled down on prioritizing their families—particularly their children—over friendships. One 2013
Pew Research study
found that 49% of parents report spending more time with their kids than their own parents did, while 33% report spending the same amount of time, and 18% report spending less time. These trends reflect a cultural shift towards “intensive parenting.” A child’s achievements are an extension of their parents’ competence, which fuels an arms race of over-scheduling, constant supervision, and exhaustive emotional labor. data.title: Accidentally Turing-Complete
data.author: bschne
data.article_summary:
本文列举了一些意外具有图灵完备性的系统和例子，尽管它们最初并非为此设计。包括：

1. **C++模板**和**TypeScript类型系统**：它们通过复杂的类型操作实现了图灵完备。
2. **Java泛型**：尽管Java试图修正C++的问题，最终也变得图灵完备。
3. **X86 MOV指令**：仅使用MOV指令也能实现图灵机，甚至有基于此的编译器和无分支版《DOOM》游戏。
4. **X86 MMU**：通过页故障处理实现简单机器。
5. **《万智牌》**：卡牌规则复杂到可以实现图灵完备性，并有相关论文和实际卡牌演示。
6. **HTML5+CSS3**：新版本可通过复杂组合实现规则110自动机。
7. **《Minecraft》和《矮人要塞》**：游戏内的逻辑构建展示了图灵完备性，如在《矮人要塞》中实现《太空侵略者》游戏。
8. **SQL**：通过公共表表达式和窗口功能，SQL也可图灵完备。
9. **C预处理器**：在特定循环条件下具有图灵完备性。
10. **Apache重写规则**：尽管有限制，但其URL重写系统是图灵完备的。
11. **《Pokemon Yellow》**：通过特定操作和漏洞实现图灵完备性。

这些例子展示了不同系统在非传统情况下意外具备的计算能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同系统或语言的图灵完备性及其限制

不同观点：
• [a_cardboard_box] 认为 Rule 110 只有在拥有无限大的单元数组并能用无限重复的模式初始化时，才是图灵完备的。他指出，HTML+CSS 只能处理固定大小的数组，而在图灵完备的语言中，如果程序在一台机器上内存不足，可以在更大内存的机器上运行同一代码而不需要修改代码。对于固定长度的 Rule 110，如果需要更多内存，则必须修改代码。

• [panstromek] 对某些语言或系统的图灵完备性提出不同看法，认为 TypeScript 的类型系统在尝试描述动态类型语言时，显然是图灵完备的，尽管有人可能认为这是“偶然的”图灵完备。

• [WalterGR] 引用了 x86 MOV 指令的一个例子，提到基于该指令的 MOV-only DOOM 游戏，渲染一帧需要大约7个小时，暗示某些图灵完备的实现可能在实际应用中受限，比如性能问题。

补充讨论：
• 图灵完备性的实际应用限制：从 [a_cardboard_box] 的评论中可以看出，虽然某些系统在理论上是图灵完备的，但实际使用中可能受到内存或数组大小的限制，需要权衡代码修改和硬件资源。
• 对某些系统图灵完备性的争议：[panstromek] 提到 TypeScript 的图灵完备性可能并非偶然，显示出对某些系统是否属于“真正”图灵完备的争议。
• 性能问题：[WalterGR] 的例子展示了某些图灵完备实现可能在性能上存在显著问题，影响其实际可用性。

43811561.article_content:
Some things were not supposed to be
Turing-complete
.
This is a collection of such accidents.
Stuff which is somehow limited
(stack overflows, arbitrary configuration, etc)
is still considered Turing complete,
since all "physical" Turing machines are resource limited.
C++ Templates
Although they were initially not supposed to,
C++ templates are Turing-complete.
For proof look at this
paper (pdf)
.
TypeScript Type System
In a very similar fashion to C++,
the type system of TypeScript can be used to
implement a prime check
.
Java Generics
Although Java set out to fix the errors of C++,
it also fell into Turing-completeness eventually.
Radu Grigore built a  parser generator for fluent interfaces
.
X86 Mov
The paper
mov is Turing-complete
starts as this:
It is well-known that the x86 instruction set is baroque,
overcomplicated, and redundantly redundant.
We show just how much fluff it has by demonstrating that it remains
Turing-complete when reduced to just one instruction.
It inspired
movfuscator
,
the single instruction C compiler.
Building on this,
there is
a branchless, mov-only version of the classic DOOM video game
.
This is thought to be entirely secure against the Meltdown and Spectre
CPU vulnerabilities, which require speculative execution
on branch instructions.
The mov-only DOOM renders approximately one frame every 7 hours,
so playing this version requires somewhat increased patience.
X86 MMU
The page fault handling in X86 can be used to
implement
a simple machine.
Basically, a page fault pushes a word to the stack, which might underflow generating another trap.
This mechanism provides a "subtract and branch if less than or equal to zero" instruction.
Enough to implement a Turing machine.
Also see
the talk
.
Magic: The Gathering
Magic is a card game.
Apparently
,
the rules are complex enough to reach Turing-completeness.
There is even a paper about it:
Magic: The Gathering is Turing Complete
Magic: The Gathering is a popular and famously complicated trading card game about magical combat. In this paper we show that optimal play in real-world Magic is at least as hard as the Halting Problem, solving a problem that has been open for a decade. To do this, we present a methodology for embedding an arbitrary Turing machine into a game of Magic such that the first player is guaranteed to win the game if and only if the Turing machine halts. Our result applies to how real Magic is played, can be achieved using standard-size tournament-legal decks, and does not rely on stochasticity or hidden information. Our result is also highly unusual in that all moves of both players are forced in the construction. This shows that even recognising who will win a game in which neither player has a non-trivial decision to make for the rest of the game is undecidable. We conclude with a discussion of the implications for a unified computational theory of games and remarks about the playability of such a board in a tournament setting.
And here is someone actual doing it with real cards.
HTML5 + CSS3
While older HTML/CSS versions are not,
with some new additions, you
can
write a
rule 110 automaton
.
The original page has
moved here
and there is also
Github
and a video.
Minecraft
Maybe this one was intentional,
but the complexity of the computers people build in Minecraft is impressive.
Dwarf Fortress
In a similar vein,
the infamous Dwarf Fortress game provides various ways
to build logical AND, OR, or NAND gates for
computing
.
A very impressive example is a space invaders game
in the following video.
Doom
Doom is probably the most widely ported game
but so far nobody has ported anything
onto
Doom.
Jared Candelaria shows how to build all kinds of gates
as Doom levels and monsters as signals
.
Unfortunately, a maximum of 65535 gates
is a very small target.
SQL
SQL is usually not considered to be Turing-complete.
However, with the features Common Table Expressions and Windowing,
SQL is Turing Complete
.
The proof is in
these slides
.
Also, look a
Mandelbrot in SQL:2008
.
A
broader exploration of various SQL-turing-machines
was done by Fabien Coelho.
(C Preprocessor)
The C preprocessor is only Turing-complete
if executed in a loop
which feeds the output to the input ad infinitum.
An example has won the
IOCCC 2001
contest.
Look into the herrmann1 entry.
Nonetheless included in this list for coolness.
Apache Rewrite Rules
Apache comes with the mod_rewrite plugin to rewrite URLs.
These rules ultimately are a Turing complete
string rewrite system
.
Though the default configuration sets very low limits to recursion.
(Pokemon Yellow)
A Pokemon game, which is
finished in 1minute 36seconds
.
The interesting point about this speedrun is the bug it exploits.
Turns out the game logic itself is Turing-complete in the sense
that you can write assembly by filling the player inventory appropriately.
Executing this assembly is not part of the (intended) game though.
I consider it close enough to keep it on this list.

43811561.article_summary:
本文列举了一些意外具有图灵完备性的系统和例子，尽管它们最初并非为此设计。包括：

1. **C++模板**和**TypeScript类型系统**：它们通过复杂的类型操作实现了图灵完备。
2. **Java泛型**：尽管Java试图修正C++的问题，最终也变得图灵完备。
3. **X86 MOV指令**：仅使用MOV指令也能实现图灵机，甚至有基于此的编译器和无分支版《DOOM》游戏。
4. **X86 MMU**：通过页故障处理实现简单机器。
5. **《万智牌》**：卡牌规则复杂到可以实现图灵完备性，并有相关论文和实际卡牌演示。
6. **HTML5+CSS3**：新版本可通过复杂组合实现规则110自动机。
7. **《Minecraft》和《矮人要塞》**：游戏内的逻辑构建展示了图灵完备性，如在《矮人要塞》中实现《太空侵略者》游戏。
8. **SQL**：通过公共表表达式和窗口功能，SQL也可图灵完备。
9. **C预处理器**：在特定循环条件下具有图灵完备性。
10. **Apache重写规则**：尽管有限制，但其URL重写系统是图灵完备的。
11. **《Pokemon Yellow》**：通过特定操作和漏洞实现图灵完备性。

这些例子展示了不同系统在非传统情况下意外具备的计算能力。
43811561.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同系统或语言的图灵完备性及其限制

不同观点：
• [a_cardboard_box] 认为 Rule 110 只有在拥有无限大的单元数组并能用无限重复的模式初始化时，才是图灵完备的。他指出，HTML+CSS 只能处理固定大小的数组，而在图灵完备的语言中，如果程序在一台机器上内存不足，可以在更大内存的机器上运行同一代码而不需要修改代码。对于固定长度的 Rule 110，如果需要更多内存，则必须修改代码。

• [panstromek] 对某些语言或系统的图灵完备性提出不同看法，认为 TypeScript 的类型系统在尝试描述动态类型语言时，显然是图灵完备的，尽管有人可能认为这是“偶然的”图灵完备。

• [WalterGR] 引用了 x86 MOV 指令的一个例子，提到基于该指令的 MOV-only DOOM 游戏，渲染一帧需要大约7个小时，暗示某些图灵完备的实现可能在实际应用中受限，比如性能问题。

补充讨论：
• 图灵完备性的实际应用限制：从 [a_cardboard_box] 的评论中可以看出，虽然某些系统在理论上是图灵完备的，但实际使用中可能受到内存或数组大小的限制，需要权衡代码修改和硬件资源。
• 对某些系统图灵完备性的争议：[panstromek] 提到 TypeScript 的图灵完备性可能并非偶然，显示出对某些系统是否属于“真正”图灵完备的争议。
• 性能问题：[WalterGR] 的例子展示了某些图灵完备实现可能在性能上存在显著问题，影响其实际可用性。

data.title: Avoiding skill atrophy in the age of AI
data.author: NotInOurNames
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）对技能学习与运用的影响，包括其潜在的技能退化、知识同质化以及对生产力的影响。

不同观点：
• LLM作为学习和提升的工具：
  - LLM帮助理解复杂问题，验证解决方案，并促进自学（gchamonlive）。
  - 使用LLM需要更好的解释能力和问题理解，推动程序员在编码前深入思考（rjknight）。
  - LLM可以作为练习和提高技能的工具，如Leetcode训练（leonidasv）。

• LLM带来的技能退化与依赖：
  - 依赖LLM可能导致基本技能的退化，例如地图阅读技能因GPS普及而减弱（afiodorov）。
  - LLM可能会加剧知识同质化，导致局部环境问题的通用解决方案缺乏实际感官基础（bluetomcat）。
  - 依赖外部工具（如AI）进行思考可能降低个人创造性思维和独立解决问题的能力（randcraw, AdventureMouse）。

• LLM对生产力和就业市场的影响：
  - 使用LLM可以提高生产力，但可能以降低劳动力成本为目标，而非单纯提高生产力（stego-tech）。
  - LLM可能导致程序员技能的二极分化，能够测量和理解问题的工程师与依赖AI的开发者之间（austin-cheney）。

• LLM对个人成就感和幸福感的影响：
  - 自己动手做事的成就感（如编程、建造）是幸福感和自我价值的核心，AI可能削弱这种体验（sunshine-o）。
  - 个人兴趣与生产力工作的交集是保持工作愉悦的关键，避免技能退化（Saigonautica）。

补充讨论：
- LLM并非全新的技能退化起点，搜索引擎和代码片段复制粘贴早已开始影响技能水平（trollbridge）。
- 担忧社会整体知识水平的下降，AI工具可能导致社会知识权力集中于少数人手中（stego-tech, gherkinnn）。
- 对未来生产力提升的怀疑，认为AI可能导致平均智商下降（bgwalter）。

data.title: Programming in D: Tutorial and Reference
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 《Programming in D》是Ali Çehreli编写的一本关于D语言的教程和参考书，涵盖D语言的基础与高级特性。书籍提供了多种格式，包括纸质书、Kindle电子书、互动课程、以及免费的PDF等。内容从基本的"Hello World"程序开始，逐步介绍D语言的基本语法和概念，如变量、数据类型、控制结构、函数、异常处理、模板、并发编程等。书中还详细讲解了D语言独特的功能，如关联数组、契约编程、UFCS（通用函数调用语法）、混合编程等。此外，书中包含大量代码示例和练习，适合从初学者到高级开发者的学习需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：D语言的优劣、使用体验及其生态系统

不同观点：
• [usrbinenv] 认为D语言及其替代品（如Crystal、Dart）在技术上优于当前更流行的语言（如Python、TypeScript、Go）。虽然承认流行语言的生态更丰富，但坚持认为从语言设计角度，D等更优越。
• [WalterBright] 分享了他在D编译器上的开发工作，表明对D语言的技术细节有浓厚兴趣，但未直接评价其优劣。
• [zascrash] 和 [Daunk] 都表示D语言未得到应有的认可，希望有更多大公司支持该语言。
• [kingbob000] 表示在大学课程中使用过D语言，但如今难以找到使用场景，暗示其实用性较低。
• [croemer] 提到LDC2编译器在macOS上的崩溃问题，表明D语言工具链存在技术问题。
• [nerdralph] 指出D语言的库较少，尤其是与Perl、Python、C++相比，限制了其实用性。
• [jpecar] 提到D语言在多核CPU上的运行时问题，进一步提出了其在大规模系统上的适用性问题。
• [Defletter] 分享了使用D语言开发的负面体验，特别是工具链不完善、编译问题以及对mixins和属性的处理不当，最终选择了其他语言。

补充讨论：
• D语言的工具链问题：[Defletter] 详细描述了使用D语言时遇到的工具链问题，包括多个竞争的编译器（dmd、ldc、gdc）以及IDE插件无法处理mixins和属性等问题，表明D语言在开发体验上存在不足。
• 生态系统问题：[pmags] 提到十年前使用D语言时标准库存在缺陷，并询问近几年D语言的生态是否有显著改善，表明生态系统一直是D语言的短板。
• 实际应用问题：[shoozza] 提出了D语言是否适合创建极小可执行文件的问题，引发了对D语言在特定场景（如游戏开发）中的适用性讨论。

争议焦点：
• D语言的技术优越性与其生态系统的不足之间的矛盾。虽然一些开发者认为D语言在设计上优于其他语言，但其工具链和库的缺乏限制了其实际应用。

• D语言的技术优越性与其生态系统的不足之间的矛盾。虽然一些开发者认为D语言在设计上优于其他语言，但其工具链和库的缺乏限制了其实际应用。

data.title: Reading RSS content is a skilled activity
data.author: d0liver
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了互联网从早期 quirky 和利他主义的状态，演变为如今以吸引用户注意力为核心的经济模式，这种模式往往对用户产生有害影响。广告商通过算法增加用户参与度，却不关心用户体验。文章提出通过 RSS 技术重新掌控注意力，强调 RSS 阅读器的使用体验与社交媒体不同，用户自主决定阅读内容。作者建议通过信任链来筛选内容，从信任的来源开始订阅，再根据其推荐扩展，逐步打造个性化且多元化的内容库。使用 RSS 阅读器不仅是内容聚合，更是一种技能和习惯，通过主动筛选内容，用户能更好地管理自己的注意力。

43799697.article_content:
Shit's gotten weird out there. The internet has devolved from something that was mostly quirky and altruistic to something that, in many ways, is straight-up evil. Companies have commoditized user attention through an economic framework that is completely divorced from the user's experience: Advertisers go to some ad platform, set up a few tags, and third parties shill for them without knowing anything about advertiser or user. The user's experience is determined by some algorithm whose sole purpose is to increase engagement, so the effects on the user are harmful and unknown, and advertisers don't care.
Enter RSS: An opportunity to reclaim your attention through simple and open tech. Unfortunately, I've bailed on all of my attempts at using RSS readers up to this point because there's simply too much content to sift through. But, I'm finally realizing what was right in front of my face: The experience of using an RSS reader
is
and
should be
characteristically different than using other forms of social media. With an RSS reader, you decide what you see; in order to
decide
you must start with something
undecided
meaning
unfiltered
.
So, how do we decide and filter for ourselves? My favored approach is fairly old fashioned: Chains of trust. We start by finding someone whose
judgement
we trust and subscribing to their feed, and then we find out who they trust and subscribe to their feed, and so on. Part of the
judgement
that we're looking for in these trustees is not simply whether or not content is
accurate
but whether or not it is worth our
attention
. Over time, we can curate our little garden of content, make it diverse, and eliminate unnecessary noise. But, much like a real garden, pruning and weeding is essential and intentional. So, using an RSS reader is more than having a nice aggregator: It's a skill and a routine. And that's also where the magic lies because it's that very process of engaging with content and deciding whether or not it has value to you that makes using an RSS reader a better experience and one where you own your attention.

data.title: What If We Could Rebuild Kafka from Scratch?
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary:
Gunnar Morling探讨了如果从零开始重建Kafka，哪些特性和功能是理想的。他提到KIP-1150和AutoMQ的Kafka fork，这些项目旨在通过分离存储与计算以及支持对象存储（如S3）来提升Kafka在云环境中的表现。Morling提出了几个关键改进：

1. **取消分区**：分区曾用于扩展，但在云存储中不再必要。应关注消息键的全局或同键排序，而非分区的无关消息排序。
2. **以键为中心的访问**：支持高效访问和重放同键消息，实现动态消费者增减，解决头部阻塞问题。
3. **主题层次**：像Solace系统一样，通过结构化路径标识消息，便于客户端订阅。
4. **并发控制**：通过消息键的乐观锁定防止过时数据写入。
5. **Broker端 schema 支持**：将schema支持作为一级概念，提升用户体验并兼容不同存储格式。
6. **可扩展性和可插拔性**：借鉴Postgres和Kubernetes，通过定义扩展点实现系统定制。

这些改进旨在构建更高效、灵活的云原生事件日志系统。

不同观点：

• Frklem从哲学角度反思技术对象的存在方式，认为技术改进应有更深的反思和目的。
• Elvircrn惊讶于讨论中未提及Redpanda。
• Selkin认为Kafka的最大优势在于其广泛的生态系统，尽管有设计上的不足，但生态系统的价值使得替换Kafka变得困难。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提及Kafka的复杂性和适用场景问题，并提出了多种替代方案（如NATS、Pulsar、SQS/SNS、Redpanda、Fluvio）。
• 争议的焦点在于Kafka的架构是否能够满足各种需求，尤其是在消息键确认、排序和消费者并发控制方面。
• 有对技术改进的哲学反思，强调在技术方案选择中应考虑实际需求和目的。
• 提到的新技术和项目（如Northguard、Fluvio、Redpanda）提供了可能的未来发展方向。

Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
What If We Could Rebuild Kafka From Scratch?
Posted at Apr 24, 2025
Update April 25: This post is being discussed on
Hacker News
,
lobste.rs
, and
/r/apachekafka
The last few days I spent some time digging into the recently announced
KIP-1150
("Diskless Kafka"), as well
AutoMQ’s Kafka fork
, tightly integrating Apache Kafka and object storage, such as S3. Following the example set by WarpStream, these projects aim to substantially improve the experience of using Kafka in cloud environments, providing better elasticity, drastically reducing cost, and paving the way towards native lakehouse integration.
This got me thinking, if we were to start all over and develop a durable cloud-native event log from scratch—​Kafka.next if you will—​which traits and characteristics would be desirable for this to have? Separating storage and compute and object store support would be table stakes, but what else should be there? Having used Kafka for many years for building event-driven applications as well as for running realtime ETL and change data capture pipelines, here’s my personal wishlist:
Do away with partitions:
topic partitions were crucial for scaling purposes when data was stored on node-local disks, but they are not required when storing data on effectively infinitely large object storage in the cloud. While partitions also provide ordering guarantees, this never struck me as overly useful from a client perspective. You either want to have global ordering of all messages on a given topic, or (more commonly) ordering of all messages with the same key. In contrast, defined ordering of otherwise unrelated messages whose key happens to yield the same partition after hashing isn’t that valuable, so there’s not much point in exposing partitions as a concept to users.
Key-centric access:
instead of partition-based access, efficient access and replay of all the messages with one and the same key would be desirable. Rather than coarse-grained scanning of all the records on a given topic or partition, let’s have millions of entity-level streams! Not only would this provide access exactly to the subset of data you need, it would also let you increase and decrease the number of consumers dynamically based on demand, not hitting the limits of a pre-defined partition count. Key-level streams (with guaranteed ordering) would be a perfect foundation for
Event Sourcing
architectures as well as actor-based and agentic systems. In addition, this approach largely solves the problem of head-of-line blocking found in partition based systems with cumulative acknowledgements: if a consumer can’t process a particular message, this will only block other messages with the same key (which oftentimes is exactly what you’d want), while all other messages are not affected. Rather than coarse-grained partitions, individual messages keys are becoming the failure domain.
Topic hierarchies:
available in systems like
Solace
, topic hierarchies promote parts of the message payload into structured path-like topic identifiers, allowing for clients to subscribe to arbitrary sub sets of all the available streams based on patterns in an efficient way, without requiring brokers to deserialize and parse entire messages.
Means of concurrency control:
As is, using Kafka as a system of record can be problematic as you can’t prevent writing messages which are based on an outdated view of the stored data. Concurrency control, for instance via optimistic locking of message keys, would help to detect and fence off concurrent conflicting writes. That way, when a message gets acknowledged successfully, it is guaranteed that it has been produced seeing the latest state of that key, avoiding lost updates.
Broker-side schema support:
Kafka treats messages as opaque byte arrays with arbitrary content, requiring out-of-bands propagation of message schemas to consumers. This can be especially problematic when erroneous (or malicious) producers send non-conformant data. Also, without additional tooling, the current architecture prevents Kafka data from being written to open table formats such as Apache Iceberg. For all these reasons, Kafka is used with a schema registry most of the time, but making schema support a first-class concept would allow for better user ergonomics—​for instance, Kafka could expose
AsyncAPI-compatible metadata
out of the box—​and also open the door for storing data in different ways, for instance in a columnar representation.
Extensibility and pluggability:
a common trait of many successful open-source projects like Postgres or Kubernetes is their extensibility. Users and integrators can customize the behavior of the system by providing implementations of well-defined extension points and plug-in contracts, rather than by modifying the system’s core itself (following the
Open-closed principle
). This would enable for in

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者通过神经网络将一段森林小径的视频转化为一个可探索的虚拟世界。该世界完全由神经网络生成，无需传统的三维建模、光影代码或动画脚本。用户可以在网页浏览器中离线探索这个神经网络生成的世界。作者首先录制了包含手机运动数据的视频，然后训练神经网络模拟这些视频帧之间的变化。最初的尝试结果不尽如人意，世界看起来像是一团混乱的“汤”。经过多次改进，包括增加控制信息、内存和多尺度处理，作者最终创建了一个较为稳定且可玩的虚拟森林世界。该项目展示了神经网络在构建可交互虚拟环境方面的潜力，特别是可以从任何视频文件中生成独特的虚拟世界。

43798757.article_content:
World Emulation via Neural Network
25 April 2025
I turned a forest trail near my apartment into a playable neural world.
You can explore that world in your web browser
by clicking right here
:
By "neural world", I mean that the entire thing is a neural network generating new images based on previous images + controls. There is no level geometry, no code for lighting or shadows, no scripted animation. Just a neural net in a loop.
By "in your web browser" I mean this world runs locally, in
your
web browser. Once the world has loaded, you can continue exploring even in Airplane Mode.
So, why bother creating a world this way? There are some interesting conceptual reasons (I'll get to them later), but my main goal was just to outdo a prior post.
See,
three years ago
, I got a simple two-dimensional video game world to run in-browser by training a neural network to mimic gameplay videos from YouTube.
Mimicking a 2D video game world was cute, but ultimately kind of pointless;
existing video games already exist and we can already emulate them just fine.
The wonderful, unique, exciting property of neural worlds is that they can be constructed from any video file,
not just screen recordings of old video games.
My previous post didn't really get this across.
So for this post, to demonstrate what makes neural networks truly special,
I wanted to train a neural network on gameplay videos of the actual world.
Recording data
To begin this project, I walked through a forest trail, recording videos with my phone,
using a customized camera app which also recorded my phone's motion.
I collected ~15 minutes of video and motion recordings. I've visualized motion as a "walking" control stick on the left and a "looking" control stick on the right.
Back at home, I transferred the recordings to my laptop, and shuffled them into a list of (
previous frame, control
→
next frame
) pairs just like my previous game-emulation dataset.
Now, all I needed to do was train a neural network to mimic the behavior of these input→output pairs. I already had working code from my previous game-emulation project,
so I tried rerunning that code to establish a baseline.
Training baselines
Applying my previous game-emulation-via-neural-network recipe to this new dataset produced, regrettably, a sort of interactive forest-flavored soup.
My neural network couldn't predict the actual next frame accurately,
and it couldn't make up new details fast enough to compensate,
so the resulting world collapsed even if I gave it a running start by initializing from real video frames:
Undaunted, I started work on a new version of the neural world training code.
Upgrading the training recipe
To help my network understand real-world video, I made the following upgrades:
Adding more control information.
I upgraded the "control" network input from simple 2D controls to more-informative 3D (
6DoF
) controls.
Adding more memory.
I upgraded the "memory" network input from a single frame to 32 frames (using lower resolution for the older frames).
Adding multiple scales.
I restructured the network to process all inputs across multiple resolutions, instead of a fixed 1/8 resolution.
These upgrades let me stave off soupification enough to get a half-baked demo:
This was  significant progress. Unfortunately, the world was still pretty melty,
so I started work on a second batch of improvements (more daunted this time).
Upgrading the training recipe more
This time, I left the inputs/outputs as-is and focused on finding incremental improvements to the training procedure. Here's a mercifully-abbreviated montage:
The biggest jumps in quality came from:
Making the network bigger
: I added even more layers of neural network processing, while striving to maintain a somewhat-playable FPS.
Picking a better training objective
: I adjusted training to put less emphasis on
detail prediction
and more emphasis on
detail generation
.
Training longer
: I trained the network longer on a selected subset of video frames to try and eke out the highest-quality results.
Here's a summary of the final forest world recipe:
Dataset
: 22,814 frames (30FPS SDR video, timestamped ARKit poses) captured at Marymoor Park Audobon Bird Loop with iPhone 13 Pro.
Inputs
:
3x4-element relative camera pose, 2-element gravity-relative roll/pitch, relative time delta, valid/augmented bit,
4 past-frame TCHW memory buffers (32×3×3×4, 16×3×12×16, 8×3×48×64, 4×3×192×256),
4 U(0, 1) single-channel noise tensors at each spatial scale (like StyleGAN).
Model
: Asymmetric (decoder-heavy) 4-scale UNet with reduced-size full-resolution decoder block.
~5M trainable parameters, ~1 GFLOP per generated 192×256 frame.
Training
: AdamW constant LR + SWA, L1 + adversarial loss, stability fixes from the game-emulation recipe, around ~100 GPU-hours (~$100 USD).
Inference
: Control-conditioned sequential autoregression with 60FPS cap, preprocessing in JS, network in ONNX Runtime Web's WebGL backend.
Whew. So, let's return to the original que

data.title: AI Horseless Carriages
data.author: petekoomen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI功能在各种产品中的实用性、用户需求以及商业化动机

不同观点：
• joshstrange认为，目前大多数AI功能显得多余且无用，特别是在价格上涨的情况下。他只对编码相关的AI工具（如Copilot、Claude Code）感兴趣，对其他AI增强功能持怀疑态度。
• tlogan指出，AI无法解决用户不清楚自己目标的问题，反而可能放大这种模糊性。虽然AI降低了新工具的学习曲线，但它也可能阻碍用户对工具的深度掌握和真实问题的解决。
• mNovak批评了一些明显但无用的AI功能，如Gmail中的“总结此邮件”按钮，认为许多有用的AI功能没有被注意到，因为它们不引人注目。
• crote认为，最有用的AI功能往往被忽视，因为它们不具备视觉冲击力，且难以商业化。这些功能更注重实用性而非华丽的表现。
• oceanplexian讨论了AI生成内容的可调性，指出通过微调和提示，AI可以生成非常接近人类风格的内容，但大公司可能因安全考虑而选择保留一些机械化的特征。
• pmarreck提出，AI可能将人类转变为“工作审核者”而非“工作执行者”，因为AI能够自动生成和审查工作成果，用户只需最后批准。
• throwaway2037将使用低效AI功能比作管理表现不佳的员工，强调直接完成任务可能比使用AI更高效。
• kristjank对AI生成消息的非个人化表示担忧，认为这剥夺了个人表达思想和情感的能力。
• benterris反对AI代写个人消息，认为这降低了交流的真实性和意义。
• Karrot_Kream认为，许多公司为了追逐AI热潮而匆忙添加无用的AI功能，以提升增长数据，而非真正改善产品。
• kkoncevicius预测，AI应用的终极形态可能会完全消除人类之间的互动，因为AI能够自我生成和审核内容。
• dvt呼吁新的UX/UI范式，强调AI应在用户意识到需求之前提供解决方案，并批评当前的AI产品过于关注附加功能而非整体产品创新。
• kfajdsl指出，大公司如微软、谷歌、苹果在AI整合方面表现不佳，而个人开发者可能在一天内就能实现更实用的AI功能。
• minimaxir批评AI生成的预填充回复功能，认为这在社交媒体上可能增加低质量的自动化互动，而在邮件等更私密的交流中尤为明显。
• darth_avocado认为，谷歌等公司不推出自动阅读和分类邮件的AI功能是因为这会影响其广告收入，只有当他们找到新的盈利模式时，才会推出此类功能。

补充讨论：
• AI功能的实用性与商业动机之间的冲突，许多评论提到公司因追逐市场热潮而添加无用的AI功能。
• AI生成内容的个性化与非个人化问题，部分用户担心AI会削弱人类交流的真实性。
• 对AI在提高生产力与阻碍深度掌握之间的矛盾看法，有些观点认为AI虽降低了学习门槛，但可能阻碍用户对工具的深入理解。
• 对AI未来发展的预测，包括完全消除人类互动的可能性以及对新UX/UI范式的需求。

data.title: Did 5G Kill the IMSI Catcher?
data.author: skramace
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了IMSI捕获器（IMSI catcher）这一长期存在的移动网络安全漏洞，以及5G技术是否解决了这一问题。IMSI（国际移动用户识别码）是每个手机用户的身份标识，用于连接SIM卡和用户账户。IMSI捕获器分为主动和被动两种，主动捕获器通过模拟基站获取IMSI，但违法且易被检测；被动捕获器则通过收集信号在用户设备与基站注册时截获IMSI，更为隐蔽。

尽管2G到4G网络中，IMSI常以明文传输，易被截获，但5G引入了改进的安全机制，理论上减少了IMSI的暴露。然而，5G的解决方案并不完美，仍存在可被利用的漏洞。文章最后指出，尽管5G在安全性上有显著提升，但IMSI捕获器并未完全消失，仍是一个值得关注的安全问题。

Did 5G kill the IMSI catcher?
A primer on one of the oldest cellular vulnerabilities
April 10, 2025
by Mark Santorello, Senior Cyber Engineer
You dial into your Zoom meeting while sitting on a moving train. Your mobile device (i.e., User Equipment, UE) must seamlessly switch towers as you go in and out of range. This concept, called
mobility,
remains a central requirement for mobile networks, but it’s also a central security vulnerability.
You see, you may have just been hacked while leisurely zooming on said train – and you’d never know it.
The GSM (better known as 2G) protocol has
a security vulnerability that exposes a user’s personal identifier (IMSI) in the clear, allowing for attribution and geolocation.
This vulnerability is also in the UMTS (a.k.a. 3G) spec, and in the LTE (4G) spec. While the vulnerability was finally addressed in NR (5G), it’s imperfect and remains an exploitable 5G network vulnerability… and my favorite cybersecurity topic.
In this article, I’ll introduce this long-standing security exploit, known as an IMSI catcher, discuss some high-level technical aspects regarding 2G–4G IMSI catchers, then finish with 5G security improvements and the possibility of 5G IMSI catchers.
What is an IMSI?
Every account on a cellular network has a unique identifier to connect a SIM card to a credit card, and that identifier is called the International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI, pronounced “IM-zee”). This number contains 3 pieces of information: the Mobile Country Code (MCC) of the issuing network operator, the Mobile Network Code (MNC) of the issuing network operator, and a unique number that only exists for that SIM card. The IMSI is ultimately used to make sure you paid your bill and that you’re allowed to register onto a network.
What is an IMSI catcher?
An IMSI catcher is a tool that collects cellular signals and decodes packets to access and save off the IMSI. There are two types of IMSI catchers:
active and passive.
Active IMSI Catcher
Also known as a cell station simulator or rogue base station, an active IMSI catcher is the more effective of the two. The downside is that it requires RF transmission, which violates FCC laws (and international equivalents) and is detectable.
Passive IMSI Catcher
This type requires a lot more planning and may not yield as many IMSIs. However, it’s undetectable (from an RF perspective) and reflects a true account of the network without interference.
To use an analogy,
active
IMSI catchers are like standing outside of the grocery store with an official-looking outfit and asking for people’s licenses to write down the number; it may work until someone with a badge shows up.
On the other hand,
passive
IMSI catchers are like sitting behind the one-way glass by the checkout counter and taking a photo of everyone’s licenses when they open their wallets – difficult to detect and not illegal because it’s in plain sight (probably… I’m not a lawyer and this isn’t legal advice).
How does an IMSI catcher work?
(NB: The remainder of this article refers exclusively to passive IMSI catchers.)
A UE (User Equipment, like your smartphone) is constantly performing selection, reselection, and registration procedures to maintain mobility and access to the cellular network. These processes are extremely complicated at the technical level, yet conceptually they’re very simple.
After selecting a cell tower, based on measurements and control information, the UE sends a request to attach to a cell tower.
If the UE is allowed to attach, the cell tower and UE go back and forth a few times to negotiate some parameters, finalizing with the UE sending its IMSI.
The cell tower starts a new back-and-forth with the network to establish whether or not the IMSI is valid, active, and paid.
If the UE is allowed on the network, the cell tower initiates the authentication process, and everything from here on out is encrypted.
This would be the end of the story, were it not for mobility. Again, mobility is a feature, as well as a network vulnerability. Every time the UE switches to another tower, it must repeat the registration process. (Ok, not EVERY time, but every time that the UE is in IDLE mode, which is most of the time. Handover is a whole other discussion.)
To minimize the number of times a UE registers using an unencrypted IMSI, the network issues a Temporary Mobile Subscriber Identity (TMSI, pronounced “TIM-zee”). The TMSI is issued over an encrypted connection and associated with the IMSI on the network side. For the sake of this article, we’ll consider the TMSI to be an unexploitable solution (…it’s not).
There are 3 ways to catch an IMSI:
LOCATION, LOCATION, LOCATION!
As mentioned earlier, the technical aspects of developing a passive IMSI catcher are complicated. (If you’re interested in this topic, send an email to
hello@zetier.com
.) The simplified explanation is this: sometimes phones send IMSIs in cleartext, and if you’re collecting at the right place and right time, you’ll cat
43813083.article_summary:
文章讨论了IMSI捕获器（IMSI catcher）这一长期存在的移动网络安全漏洞，以及5G技术是否解决了这一问题。IMSI（国际移动用户识别码）是每个手机用户的身份标识，用于连接SIM卡和用户账户。IMSI捕获器分为主动和被动两种，主动捕获器通过模拟基站获取IMSI，但违法且易被检测；被动捕获器则通过收集信号在用户设备与基站注册时截获IMSI，更为隐蔽。

尽管2G到4G网络中，IMSI常以明文传输，易被截获，但5G引入了改进的安全机制，理论上减少了IMSI的暴露。然而，5G的解决方案并不完美，仍存在可被利用的漏洞。文章最后指出，尽管5G在安全性上有显著提升，但IMSI捕获器并未完全消失，仍是一个值得关注的安全问题。

data.article_summary: **snapDOM** 是一个高保真的 DOM 捕获工具，能够将任意 HTML 元素转换为可缩放的 SVG 图像，同时保留样式、字体、背景、阴影 DOM 内容、伪元素等。它轻量无依赖，完全基于标准 Web API，支持导出为 SVG、PNG、JPG、WebP 或 canvas。主要功能包括捕获整个 DOM 树、嵌入样式和字体、处理 Shadow DOM 和伪元素等。此外，它还具有高性能，尤其在处理大型或复杂 DOM 结构时表现突出，优于其他类似库。可通过 NPM、CDN 或脚本标签引入使用，并提供多种捕获方法如 `snapdom.toPng`、`snapdom.toCanvas` 等。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [streptomycin] 认为 SnapDOM 比 html2canvas 慢，且截图质量较差，提供了对比图片，并建议在README中明确npm包名称。

• [jdiff] 对SnapDOM如何处理CSS和SVG转换表示好奇，询问是否只支持部分样式属性并依赖浏览器计算布局。
• [simonw] 提出功能请求，希望能够自定义JPEG背景色，而不是默认的黑色。
• [krebby] 将SnapDOM与Media Capture API进行比较，讨论了序列化性能问题，并分享了自己使用CropTarget.fromElement和CaptureController的经验。
• [ashishact] 建议在README中添加图片示例以帮助用户理解。

补充讨论：
• [darrenf] 询问SnapDOM是否适合在浏览器扩展中使用，因为html2canvas不建议这样做。
• [rs186] 将SnapDOM与dom-to-image-more进行比较，询问两者的区别。
• [maxloh] 建议添加转换为PDF的功能，提到自己使用Playwright Python时遇到的问题。
• [braebo] 认为Puppeteer或Playwright的截图方法更好，并分享了自己制作CLI工具的经验。
• [badmonster] 询问SnapDOM是否支持捕获当前帧的CSS动画或仅静态状态。
• [nikeee] 询问SnapDOM是否可以在Node.js中与某些DOM polyfill一起使用。
• [andrewstuart] 建议在GitHub上添加截图示例，并提出在后端进行快照处理的可能性。

争议焦点：
• SnapDOM的性能和输出质量存在争议，部分用户认为不如html2canvas和domtoimage。
• SnapDOM在不同环境下的适用性及功能扩展存在讨论，如浏览器扩展支持、PDF转换功能等。

snapDOM
snapDOM
is a high-fidelity DOM capture tool, developed as part of the animation engine I'm developing for Zumly — a framework for creating smooth zoom-based view transitions.
It converts any HTML element into a scalable SVG image, preserving styles, fonts, backgrounds, shadow DOM content, pseudo-elements, and more.
📸 Full DOM capture
🎨 Embedded styles, pseudo-elements, and fonts
🖼️ Export to SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, or
canvas
⚡ Lightweight, no dependencies
📦 100% based on standard Web APIs

snapDOM

data.article_summary: 阅读讣告可以激发创造力，因为它们提供了与我们日常生活无关的信息，帮助我们建立远距离联想，从而产生意想不到的创意突破。作者Keith Sawyer指出，最具创意的想法往往来自 unlikely sources，而讣告正是这样一种不寻常的来源，通过展示不同的人生故事，启发新的思维方式。心理学家Sarnoff Mednick的关联理论（associative theory of creativity）表明，创造力源于将看似无关的概念连接起来，概念间的距离越大，组合就越具原创性和惊喜感。现代研究也证实了这一点，许多发明如魔术贴、便利贴等都源于这种远距离联想。因此，阅读讣告能帮助我们跳出常规思维，激发创造力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于阅读讣告的价值和用途的不同观点

不同观点：
• **jawns的观点**：数字讣告面临“讣告腐烂”的风险，可能会导致未来几代人难以获取21世纪早期的讣告信息。虽然数字讣告在分发上具有优势，但在保存方面存在问题，例如链接失效和网站关闭。

• **dredmorbius的观点**：讣告是激发思想的好工具。它们经过深入研究和精心撰写，能够将人的一生浓缩成几个段落，突出重要事迹。此外，历史采访也能提供不同的视角，帮助理解当前世界。

• **gwern的观点**：质疑通过阅读讣告来促进创造力的建议，认为缺乏实际例子支持这种观点。

• **billfruit的观点**：认为广泛阅读是有益的，但不一定通过阅读讣告来实现。推荐使用fivebooks.com等资源来寻找有趣的书籍。

• **kayo_20211030的观点**：同意阅读讣告可能有趣，但认为将其与创造力直接关联是不合理的。提出创造力与讣告之间的联系缺乏证据支持。

• **Wistar的观点**：分享了一个朋友通过阅读讣告寻找机会的例子，认为讣告可以作为一种发现新机会的工具。

• **bix6的观点**：个人经历使其对讣告相关内容有特殊感情，认为从他人生活中学习是有价值的。

• **ChrisMarshallNY的观点**：强调与背景不同的人交流可以获得新的想法，与阅读讣告有类似效果。

• **kazinator的观点**：个人规则是不关注不认识的已故人物的讣告信息。

• **ghaff的观点**：特别推荐《经济学人》的讣告，认为其值得阅读。

• **androng的观点**：认为讣告中真实人物的生活故事可以为小说创作提供灵感。

• **fnord77的观点**：质疑讣告相对于传记或其摘要是否更有价值。

• **badmonster的观点**：认为通过讣告中的生活故事来激发创造性思维是一种简单而美丽的方法。

补充讨论：
• **对讣告腐烂问题的关注**：jawns强调了数字讣告在未来保存中的潜在问题。
• **讣告与其他资源的比较**：如billfruit和fnord77提到的fivebooks.com和传记，讨论了讣告相对于其他信息源的优劣。
• **讣告的实际应用**：如Wistar和bix6分享的个人故事，展示了讣告在现实生活中的具体用途。
• **创造力与讣告的关联**：kayo_20211030和gwern对讣告是否能有效促进创造力提出质疑，认为证据不足。

争议焦点：讣告是否能有效促进创造力以及其相对于其他信息源的价值。

The Creativity Hack No One Told You About: Read the Obits
Reading obituaries can boost creativity by exposing you to distant ideas, fueling the associations that lead to unexpected breakthroughs.
The obituary section of the April 6, 2025, issue of The New York Times, with the author's highlights.
By: Keith Sawyer
A↑
A↓
Off
Bright
Dark
Blues
Gray
BeeLine Reader
uses subtle color gradients to help you read more efficiently.
I’ve been reading the obituaries for as long as I can remember. At first glance, they might seem like little more than a collection of dates and accomplishments. But for me, they’ve become a wellspring of creativity — each one a glimpse into a life I never would’ve imagined. And as decades of creativity research suggest, the most original ideas often come from the most unlikely sources.
Keith Sawyer is the author of “
Learning to See: Inside the World’s Leading Art and Design Schools.
“
That’s why one popular piece of advice for boosting creativity is to learn something new every day. But here’s the catch: This only works if that new information is
very different
from what’s already in your head. This is where most of our modern habits fall short. Internet searches, for instance, give you information that’s related to what you already know, or information that you’re already interested in. So, how do you escape that loop and stumble upon something unexpected, something you didn’t even know to look for? The obituaries, obviously — but I’ll come back to that.
In February, I
interviewed Yoed Kenett
, who studies high-level cognition and creativity, for my podcast “The Science of Creativity.” His research shows that creativity thrives on making connections between very different concepts. The core idea is simple: Our ability to create relies on prior knowledge, and our creative potential increases when that knowledge is organized into conceptual networks that help us search for, connect, and generate new ideas — what Kenett calls a “Google of the mind.”
The greater the distance between two ideas, the more original and surprising their combination tends to be.
This research goes back to the 1960s, when psychologist Sarnoff Mednick was studying patterns of thought in people diagnosed with schizophrenia. He was exploring the idea that highly creative individuals might share certain associative patterns with those diagnosed with schizophrenia, namely, the tendency to make connections between seemingly unrelated ideas. In
a classic 1962 experiment
, Mednick asked participants to say the first word that came to mind when they heard a prompt like
table
. Less creative participants tended to respond with obvious associations like
chair
or
leg
. The more creative participants gave those answers, too, but they also came up with more surprising ones, like
food
or even
mouse
.
Mednick’s observations led him to propose that highly creative people have a different kind of memory structure — one that holds a wider range of ideas and forges more unexpected connections between them. He called his theory
the associative theory of creativity
. His research showed that creative ideas are more likely to emerge from combinations of concepts that are further apart in the mind’s conceptual network. The greater the distance between two ideas, the more original and surprising their combination tends to be.
More recent research
, by Kenett and others, confirms these observations.
Some of the best-known stories of invention come from unexpected associations. Velcro, for example,
was invented
when George de Mestral was walking his hairy sheepdog through a field of burr-covered plants. It’s notoriously difficult to remove burrs from an animal’s hair, which means the animal is going to carry seeds a far distance, allowing the plant to spread more successfully. De Mestral took out a magnifying glass and saw very tiny hooks that clung to the dog’s hair. Then he made the distant connection: The burr’s mechanism, designed by nature to spread seeds, could be used to make a clothing fastener. There’s no shortage of other surprising inventions that began with distant connections:
Post-It notes
, the
X-ray
,
shatterproof glass
,
the microwave oven
,
silly putty
,
heart stents
.
The psychologist Dedre Gentner
also found
that the more conceptually distant two ideas are, the more creative their combination tends to be. For instance, she found that if you ask 100 people to imagine a chair combined with a table — two closely related items — most of them will picture something like a school desk. It’s an obvious match within the category of furniture. But if you asked 100 people to imagine a chair combined with a pony — very distant concepts — the results are far more varied and surprising: A chair you sit on while grooming a pony, one that a pony sits in, one shaped like a pony’s head, or one covered in fur.

property mapping
— when people borrow attributes like texture or shape from one concept and apply them to anoth

data.title: Libogc (Wii homebrew library) discovered to contain code stolen from RTEMS
data.author: dropbear3
data.article_summary: 该仓库存档于2025年4月27日，现为只读状态。此仓库包含Wii自制软件"The Homebrew Channel"的源代码，依赖于libogc库。然而，libogc中的部分代码被发现直接从Nintendo SDK和开源RTOS（RTEMS）窃取而来，且未保留版权信息。开发团队未解决该版权问题，导致该项目被认为涉及恶意代码盗窃和侵权。因此，当前无法合法编译此软件，且不鼓励进一步开发。该仓库包含的代码仅在Dolphin模拟器上测试过，构建过程需要devkitPPC和libogc等工具，并且仅在Linux上测试成功。所有源代码根据GNU通用公共许可证版本2或更高版本发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕libogc库的代码来源及其许可问题的争议，涉及可能的代码抄袭、道德标准、法律风险以及开源社区的反应。

不同观点：
• **msephton**：对Marcin在2025年才公开此问题表示好奇，质疑为何问题被隐瞒多年。推测可能有某种事件触发了他公开表态。

• **ndiddy**：认为公开承认使用包含反编译的Nintendo SDK代码是不明智的，但考虑到Wii已不再具有商业价值，任天堂可能不会采取行动。同时批评DevKitPro项目在许可问题上的不透明处理方式及其在商标保护上的激进态度。

• **deng**：质疑libogc开发者为何不直接使用RTEMS，推测可能与追求名气或规避GPLv2有关，并认为Wii自制程序场景的商业意义不大。

• **mubou**：认为如果指控属实，RTEMS应采取法律行动，因libogc通过Patreon接受捐赠可能涉及商业利益。希望看到此类不当行为受到法律制裁。

• **bogwog**：对指控持怀疑态度，认为现有的证据不足以证明libogc直接抄袭RTEMS代码，并建议通过详细的代码比较文章来澄清问题。

• **JoshTriplett**：对问题被揭露表示遗憾，但关注Wii自制程序加载器是否存在不依赖libogc的替代方案。

• **AshamedCaptain**：质疑当前的反向工程是否真正做到干净 room方法，指出许多项目直接使用反编译的专有代码，并对这种行为表示不满。

• **Starlevel004**：指出2000年代的Nintendo游戏机自制程序场景基于泄露的SDK是公开的秘密。

• **TuxSH**：认为这是不怀好意地揭露丑闻，指出libogc的历史问题及其在Nintendo游戏机破解场景中的常见做法，并认为这些做法在当时并无太大法律风险。

• **DidYaWipe**：询问RTEMS是什么，显示对相关技术背景缺乏了解。

• **thescriptkiddie**：表示对Nintendo代码的反向工程及GPL违规行为没有道德上的问题，尤其当涉及项目名称是“导弹系统的实时执行”时。

• **xbmcuser**：认为这是在任天堂可能采取法律行动前的一种自我保护措施。

• **londons_explore**：认为RTEMS可以用freeRTOS替代，显示对技术选择的开放态度。

• **ranger_danger**：指出自N64以来的模拟器开发普遍存在使用盗版SDK和ROM的行为，并伴随大量的内部争斗。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于libogc库是否抄袭了Nintendo SDK和RTEMS代码，以及开源项目在法律和道德上的处理方式。
• 不同的技术和法律背景使得社区内部对这一问题的看法存在显著分歧。
• 有人对指控的证据不足表示怀疑，要求更详细的分析和比较；有人则认为即使指控属实，社区对这种行为也应持宽容态度。
• 关注点还包括开源项目的许可哲学及其在法律风险下的应对策略。

ARCHIVED
This repository is archived and will not accept any further contributions.
Like most Wii homebrew software, this software depends on
libogc
.
After development of The Homebrew Channel had already started, we discovered that large portions of libogc
were stolen directly from the Nintendo SDK or games using the Nintendo SDK (decompiled and cleaned up).
We thought that at least significant parts of libogc, such as its threading implementation, were original,
and reluctantly continued to use the project while distancing ourselves from it.
It has recently been revealed that the threading/OS implementation in libogc is, in fact,
stolen from RTEMS
. The authors of libogc didn't just steal proprietary
Nintendo code, but also saw it fit to steal an
open source
RTOS and remove all attribution and copyright
information. This goes far beyond ignorance about the copyright implications of reverse engineering Nintendo
binaries, and goes straight into outright deliberate, malicious code theft and copyright infringement.
The current developers of libogc are
not interested
in
tracking this issue, finding a solution, nor informing the community of the problematic copyright status of
the project. When we filed an issue about it, they immediately closed it, replied with verbal abuse, and then
completely deleted it from public view.
For this reason, we consider it impossible to legally and legitimately compile this software at this point,
and cannot encourage any further development.
The Wii homebrew community was all built on top of a pile of lies and copyright infringement, and it's all
thanks to shagkur (who did the stealing) and the rest of the team (who enabled it and did nothing when it was discovered). Together, the developers deceived everyone into believing their work was original.
Please demand that the leaders and major contributors to console or other proprietary device SDKs and
toolkits that you use and work with do things legally, and do not tolerate this kind of behavior.
If you wish to check for yourself, for example, you can compare
this
function in libogc to
this
function in a really old version of RTEMS. While the code has been simplified and many identifiers renamed, it
is clear that the libogc version is a direct descendant of the RTEMS version. It is not possible for two code
implementations to end up this similar purely by chance.
The Homebrew Channel
This repository contains the public release of the source code for
The Homebrew Channel.
Included portions:
The Homebrew Channel
Reload stub
Banner
PyWii (includes Alameda for banner creation)
WiiPAX (LZMA executable packer)
Not included:
Installer
Note that the code in this repository differs from the source code used to build
the official version of The Homebrew Channel, which includes additional
protection features (i.e. we had to add reverse-DRM to stop scammers from
selling it).
This code is released with no warranty, and hasn't even been tested on a real
Wii, only under Dolphin (yes, this release runs under Dolphin).
Build instructions
You need devkitPPC and libogc installed, and the DEVKITPRO/DEVKITPPC environment
variables correctly set. Use the latest available versions. Make sure you have
libogc/libfat, and also install the following 3rd party libraries:
zlib
libpng
mxml
freetype
You can obtain binaries of those with
devkitPro pacman
. Simply use
sudo (dkp-)pacman -S ppc-zlib ppc-libpng ppc-mxml ppc-freetype
Additionally, you'll need the following packages on your host machine:
pycryptodomex (for PyWii)
libpng headers (libpng-dev)
gettext
sox
The build process has only been tested on Linux. You're on your own if you
want to try building this on OSX or Windows.
You'll need the Wii common key installed as ~/.wii/common-key.
First run 'make' in wiipax, then 'make' in channel. You'll find a .wad file
that you can install or directly run with Dolphin under
channel/title/channel_retail.wad. You'll also find executable binaries under
channel/channelapp, but be advised that the NAND save file / theme storage
features won't work properly if HBC isn't launched as a channel with its
correct title identity/permissions.
License
Unless otherwise noted in an individual file header, all source code in this
repository is released under the terms of the GNU General Public License,
version 2 or later. The full text of the license can be found in the COPYING
file.

• **JoshTriplett**：对问题被揭露表示遗憾，但关注Wii自制程序加载器是否存在不依赖libogc的替代方案。

• **AshamedCaptain**：质疑当前的反向工程是否真正做到干净 room方法，指出许多项目直接使用反编译的专有代码，并对这种行为表示不满。

• **Starlevel004**：指出2000年代的Nintendo游戏机自制程序场景基于泄露的SDK是公开的秘密。

• **TuxSH**：认为这是不怀好意地揭露丑闻，指出libogc的历史问题及其在Nintendo游戏机破解场景中的常见做法，并认为这些做法在当时并无太大法律风险。

• **DidYaWipe**：询问RTEMS是什么，显示对相关技术背景缺乏了解。

• **thescriptkiddie**：表示对Nintendo代码的反向工程及GPL违规行为没有道德上的问题，尤其当涉及项目名称是“导弹系统的实时执行”时。

• **xbmcuser**：认为这是在任天堂可能采取法律行动前的一种自我保护措施。

• **londons_explore**：认为RTEMS可以用freeRTOS替代，显示对技术选择的开放态度。

• **ranger_danger**：指出自N64以来的模拟器开发普遍存在使用盗版SDK和ROM的行为，并伴随大量的内部争斗。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于libogc库是否抄袭了Nintendo SDK和RTEMS代码，以及开源项目在法律和道德上的处理方式。
• 不同的技术和法律背景使得社区内部对这一问题的看法存在显著分歧。
• 有人对指控的证据不足表示怀疑，要求更详细的分析和比较；有人则认为即使指控属实，社区对这种行为也应持宽容态度。
• 关注点还包括开源项目的许可哲学及其在法律风险下的应对策略。

data.title: Reverse Geocoding Is Hard
data.author: pavel_lishin
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了将地理坐标转换为可读地址的过程，尤其是在OpenBenches项目中遇到的挑战。作者指出，虽然有诸如OpenCage、StadiaMaps等服务可以帮助将坐标转化为地址，但并非所有地点都有明确的地址，尤其是一些公园或公共区域的纪念凳。此外，地址的精确度和相关性也是个问题，例如不应将凳子与附近的住宅地址关联。

文章进一步探讨了如何构建合适的地址表示，尤其是面对不同国家和地区的地址格式差异。作者计划使用StadiaMaps获取最近的兴趣点（POI），并将名称和粗略位置组合成地址，同时考虑本地化和语言问题。最终，作者提出了一种自动化方案，并准备根据用户反馈进行调整。

总结：将地理坐标转化为可读地址存在精确度和本地化挑战，作者提出利用POI和自动化方案来解决这些问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地理编码和逆地理编码的技术挑战及其解决方案

不同观点：
• Dachande663指出，地理坐标会因大陆漂移等自然现象发生变化，如澳大利亚曾整体移动1.8米，因此依赖存储的坐标作为唯一真实来源可能存在风险。
• Andrew_eu分享了一个实际案例，涉及逆地理编码服务中的国家代码问题，通过绘制多边形并使用热修复临时解决，最终系统在几个月后被完全替换。
• Sinuhe69认为，大多数地址简单明了，少量复杂情况可以通过人工或AI解决，不需要过度追求完美方案，因为地址变化不频繁。
• Jandrewrogers强调了将地理空间坐标映射到特征空间的技术难度，指出这是AI研究中的一个难题，与实现通用人工智能（AGI）密切相关。
• AlotOfReading推荐使用Google地图解决方案，认为其提供了有效的查询和排名机制。
• Punnerud介绍了自己开发的基于OpenStreetMap和SQLite3的逆地理编码工具，节省了大量API费用。
• Andrewaylett提到，使用导航距离而非直线距离可以避免某些问题，但可能会引入其他路由相关的问题。
• Jillesvangurp分享了将OpenStreetMap数据导入Elasticsearch进行逆地理编码的经验，认为这对于邻域分组等任务效果良好。
• Vintermann讨论了地名在历史和宗教区域中的多样性问题，如挪威的多个“Engeset”和行政与教会区域的差异。
• Nerdralph指出了不同国家和地区地址表达方式的差异，以及选择权威地址数据的挑战，如加拿大官方邮政地址与911数据库地址不一致。
• Johnlk认为，这更多是一个用户体验（UX）挑战，可以通过类似Twitch众包翻译的方式解决。
• Rovr138推荐使用Geonames数据库，认为其在某些国家非常有帮助。
• Amelius建议将OpenStreetMap地址切分为短组合，进行查找以获取最佳地理匹配。
• The_arun对文章表示赞赏，认为项目简单有趣，鼓励更多人参与类似项目。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个实际案例和解决方案，包括使用Google Maps API、OpenStreetMap、Elasticsearch和Geonames数据库等不同工具。
• 争议焦点主要在于是否需要完美解决方案：一方认为需要精确处理地理数据，另一方认为简单有效的方案即可满足大部分需求。
• 还讨论了地址数据的复杂性，包括不同国家的地址格式差异、行政与宗教区域的划分以及多重官方名称等问题。
• 提出了通过技术手段（如AI、众包）解决复杂地址问题的可能性，但同时也指出了现有技术的局限性。

43812323.article_content:
My wife and I run
OpenBenches
- a crowd-sourced database of nearly 40,000 memorial benches.  Every bench is geo-tagged with a latitude and longitude. But how do you go from a string of digits to something human readable?
How do I turn
-33.755780,150.603769
into "42 Wallaby Way, Sydney, Australia"?
Luckily, that's a (somewhat) solved problem. Services like
OpenCage
,
StadiaMaps
,
OpenStreetMap
, and
Geocode.Earth
all provide APIs which transform co-ordinates into addresses.  Done! Let's go home.
Except… Not everywhere
has
an address.
Some benches are in parks
. They typically don't have a street number, but might have an interesting feature nearby to help with location. For example a statue or prominent landmark.
And… Not every address is relevant.
Some benches are on streets
. But we probably don't want to imply that the bench is
inside
or belongs to a specific nearby house.
Let's step back a bit.
Why
do we want to display a human-readable address?
We have two use-cases.
"As a visitor to the site, I want to:"
Read a (rough) textual representation of where the bench is.
Click on a component of the address to see all benches within that area.
The first is easy to explain:
The second is harder.  Suppose a bench is in Wellington, New Zealand. We want to create a URl like
openbenches.org/location/New Zealand/Wellington/
. That way, users can click on the word "Wellington" and find all the benches nearby. A user can also manually edit that URl to increase or decrease precision.
Both of these are problems of
precision
.
Let's take a look at
how one of the reverse geocoding services
deals with transforming
51.476845,-0.295296
into an address:
Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, Sandycombe Road, Kew, London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, London, Greater London, England, TW9 2EN, United Kingdom
That is
too much
address!
Yes, it is technically accurate. But it contains far too much detail for humans, the postcode is irrelevant, and the weird-subdivisions are nothing that a local person would use.
Looking at the full API response, we can see:
JSON
{
"place_id"
: 258770727,
"licence"
:
"Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0. http://osm.org/copyright"
,
"name"
:
"Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew"
,
"display_name"
:
"Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, Elizabeth Cottages, Kew, London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, London, Greater London, England, TW9 3NJ, United Kingdom"
,
"address"
:
{
"leisure"
:
"Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew"
,
"road"
:
"Elizabeth Cottages"
,
"suburb"
:
"Kew"
,
"city_district"
:
"London Borough of Richmond upon Thames"
,
"ISO3166-2-lvl8"
:
"GB-RIC"
,
"city"
:
"London"
,
"state_district"
:
"Greater London"
,
"state"
:
"England"
,
"ISO3166-2-lvl4"
:
"GB-ENG"
,
"postcode"
:
"TW9 3NJ"
,
"country"
:
"United Kingdom"
,
"country_code"
:
"gb"
}
}
Aha! Perhaps I can build a better address using just those components!
Except… Not every country has states. And not all states are used when giving addresses. Not every location is in a city. Some places have villages, prefectures, municipalities, and hamlets.
New York, New York is a valid address, but
Berlin, Berlin
is not!
There's an
address formatter by OpenCage
which is pretty sensible about stripping off irrelevant details. But, to go back to my first point, not every map location on OpenBenches is a street address and - even if it is on a street - it probably shouldn't have a house number.
Well, there's kind of a solution to that! Most mapping provider have a
POI
function - we can find nearby things of interest and use them as a location.
Here's a
bench in Cook County, Illinois, USA
. The POI address is:
JSON
{
…
"name"
:
"Central Park"
,
"coarse_location"
:
"Des Plaines, IL, USA"
,
…
}
I
assume
there's only one Central Park in Des Plaines. Do people know that "Il" is Illinois? Would "Cook County" be useful?
On the subject of localisation, not everywhere speaks English. Do I want to display addresses like "
原爆の子の像, 広島, 日本
"? How about "原爆の子の像, Hiroshima, Japan"?
We're an international site, but most benches are in Anglophone countries.
Of course, just because something is
physically
near a POI, that doesn't mean it is
logically
close to it.
Consider a bench situated
at the edge of this park
The nearest POI is "Gay's Creamery" - across the river. Is that what you'd expect?  Is there any way to easily say "if a point is
inside
an amenity* then use that as the address?
I don't want the users of our site to have to select from a list of POIs or addresses, this should be as automated as possible.
The Plan
For each bench:
Use StadiaMaps to get the nearest POI.
Get the data in English.
Concatenate the name and coarse location.
Save the "address".
Wait for complaints?
Thoughts?
Share this post on…

data.title: Unlocking Ractors: Object_id
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Ruby中的Ractors及其目前的局限性和未来改进方向。Ractors旨在将CPU密集型任务移出主线程以实现并行处理，但由于Ruby虚拟机存在全局锁和一些未解决的bug，目前在并行性能上可能还不如单线程代码。不过，开发团队正在积极修复这些问题，例如通过消除如`fstring_table`等内部数据结构的锁竞争来提升性能。尽管如此，仍有一些锁竞争点需要解决，比如`#object_id`方法。该方法原本依赖对象地址生成ID，但由于GC压缩导致对象地址变化，ID不再稳定，Aaron Patterson在Ruby 2.7中通过引入ID表解决了这一问题。文章作者计划在Ruby 3.5中正式弃用`_id2ref`方法，并继续优化Ractors的性能。

43812658.article_content:
In
a previous post about ractors
, I explained why I think it’s really unlikely you’d ever be able to run an entire application inside a ractor, but that they could
still be situationally very useful to move CPU-bound work out of the main thread, and to unlock some parallel algorithm.
But as I mentioned, this is unfortunately not yet viable because there are many known implementation bugs that can lead
to interpreter crashes, and that while they are supposed to execute in parallel, the Ruby VM still has one true global
lock that Ractors need to acquire to perform certain operations, making them often perform worse than the equivalent
single-threaded code.
But things are evolving rapidly.
Since then, there is now a team of people working on fixing exactly that: tackling known bugs and eliminating or reducing the remaining contention points.
The one example I gave to illustrate this remaining contention, was the
fstring_table
, which in short is a big internal
hash table used to deduplicate strings, which Ruby does whenever you use a String as a key in a Hash.
Because looking into that table while another Ractor is inserting a new entry would result in a crash (or worse),
until last week Ruby had to acquire the remaining VM lock whenever it touched that table.
But
John Hawthorn recently replaced it with a lock-free Hash-Set
, and now this
contention point is gone. If you re-run the JSON benchmarks from the previous post using the latest Ruby master,
the Ractor version is now twice as fast as the single-threaded version, instead of being 3 times slower.
This still isn’t perfect though, as the benchmark uses 5 ractors, hence in an ideal world should be almost 5 times faster
then the single-threaded example, so we still have a lot of work to do to eliminate or reduce the remaining contention
points.
One of such remaining contention points, that you likely didn’t suspect would be one, is
the
#object_id
method
.
And on my way back from RubyKaigi, I started working on tackling it.
But before we delve into what I plan to do about it, let’s talk about how this method came to be a contention point.
A Little Bit Of History
Up until Ruby 2.6, the
#object_id
implementation used to be quite trivial:
VALUE
rb_obj_id
(
VALUE
obj
)
{
if
(
STATIC_SYM_P
(
obj
))
{
return
(
SYM2ID
(
obj
)
*
sizeof
(
RVALUE
)
+
(
4
<<
2
))
|
FIXNUM_FLAG
;
}
else
if
(
FLONUM_P
(
obj
))
{
return
LL2NUM
((
SIGNED_VALUE
)
obj
);
}
else
if
(
SPECIAL_CONST_P
(
obj
))
{
return
LONG2NUM
((
SIGNED_VALUE
)
obj
);
}
return
LL2NUM
((
SIGNED_VALUE
)(
obj
)
/
2
);
}
Of course, it’s C so it might be a bit cryptic to the uninitiated, but in short, for the common case of a heap allocated
object, its
object_id
would be the address where the object is stored, divided by two.
So in a way,
#object_id
used to return you an actual pointer to the object.
This made implementing the lesser-known counterpart of
#object_id
,
ObjectSpace._id2ref
,
just as trivial, multiply the
object_id
by two, and here you go, you now have a pointer to the corresponding object.
s
=
"I am a string"
ObjectSpace
.
_id2ref
(
s
.
object_id
).
equal?
(
s
)
# => true
But there was actually a major problem with that implementation, which is that the Ruby heap is composed of standard-size slots.
When an object is no longer referenced, the GC reclaims the object slot and will most likely re-use it for a future object.
Hence if you were to hold onto an
object_id
, and use
ObjectSpace._id2ref
, it’s not actually certain the object you get
back is the one you got the
object_id
from, it might be a totally different object.
It also meant that if you are holding onto an
object_id
as a way to know if you’ve already seen a given object,
you may run into some false positives.
That’s why
in 2018 there was already a feature request to deprecate both
#object_id
and
_id2ref
.
Back then Matz agreed to deprecated
_id2ref
for Ruby 2.7, but pointed out that removing
#object_id
would be too much of a breaking change,
and that it is a useful API.
However, this somehow fell through the cracks, and
_id2ref
was never formally deprecated, which is
something I’d like to
do for Ruby 3.5
.
I’m not certain why
_id2ref
was added initially, given that
git blame
points to
a commit from 1999 that was generated by cvs2svn
.
But if I had to guess, I’d say it was added for
drb
which today remains the only significant user of that API in the stdlib, but
even that is about to change
.
GC Compaction
Regardless of why
_id2ref
was added, that major flaw in its design became a blocker for Aaron Patterson when
he implemented
GC compaction in Ruby 2.7
.
Since GC compaction implies that objects can be moved from one slot to another,
#object_id
could no longer be derived from
the object address, otherwise, it wouldn’t remain stable.
What Aaron did is conceptually simple:
module
Kernel
def
object_id
unless
id
=
ObjectSpace
::
OBJ_TO_ID_TABLE
[
self
]
id
=
ObjectSpace
.
next_obj_id
ObjectSpace
.
next_obj_id
+=
8
ObjectSpace
::

43812658.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Ruby中的Ractors及其目前的局限性和未来改进方向。Ractors旨在将CPU密集型任务移出主线程以实现并行处理，但由于Ruby虚拟机存在全局锁和一些未解决的bug，目前在并行性能上可能还不如单线程代码。不过，开发团队正在积极修复这些问题，例如通过消除如`fstring_table`等内部数据结构的锁竞争来提升性能。尽管如此，仍有一些锁竞争点需要解决，比如`#object_id`方法。该方法原本依赖对象地址生成ID，但由于GC压缩导致对象地址变化，ID不再稳定，Aaron Patterson在Ruby 2.7中通过引入ID表解决了这一问题。文章作者计划在Ruby 3.5中正式弃用`_id2ref`方法，并继续优化Ractors的性能。

43813046.article_content:
Watching 03 Model Sweat Over a Paul Morphy Mate-in-2
Published:
Apr 27, 2025
at
When I gave OpenAI’s 03 model a tough chess puzzle, it behaved almost like a human: thinking, doubting, retrying, and finally googling the answer. 🤣
Before I break it down step-by-step, here’s the funniest part: it spent 8 minutes calculating and pixel-measuring squares… and then cheated by using Bing.
How 03 Solves hard Chess Problems
First the Problem if you want you can try to solve it yourself
Chess Puzzle Checkmate in 2 White
This is a famous chess puzzle from Paul Morphy check out
this link
for more.
See the full conversation
here
.
1.
Careful Board Analysis
Careful Board Analysis
First, 03 spent several minutes carefully reconstructing the board based on the image.
“The board has White’s King on c8, White’s Rook on a1, and a Pawn on b6. Black’s King on a8, Bishop on b8, and Pawns on a7 and b7.”
It was being very cautious. It wanted to fully understand the position before trying any move.
Already a very agent like behavior: care first, then move.
2.
First Ideas and Doubts
It tested obvious ideas like
b7#
and
Rxa7#
, but immediately started doubting itself.
“After 1. Rxa7+, Black’s King cannot capture because of the White pawn on b6."
"But after Bxa7, it is no longer check. So it is not mate."
"1. b7+ is illegal because the pawn on b7 blocks it.”
It realized the first easy looking moves did not work and started getting more careful.
3.
Attempt to Use Python
When pure reasoning was not enough, 03 tried programming its way out of the situation.
“I should probably check using something like a chess engine to confirm.”
(tries to import
chess
module, but fails: “ModuleNotFoundError”).
Attempt to Use Python
It wanted to run a simulation, but of course, it had no real chess engine installed.
4.
Pixel-by-Pixel Image Analysis
Still stuck, it tried manually measuring the chessboard squares.
“The board is 726 pixels high, each square is about 88 pixels…"
"Coordinates for b7 would be approximately x=88–176, y=88–176.”
It was literally trying to deduce the pieces based on pixel math.
Massive stubbornness.
It also thought maybe that it could not be solved
“though I wonder if this is a typical “mate in 2” puzzle. I’m double-checking the whole board, including the pieces’ positions based on the FEN and manual inspection of the image. For example, looking at the black king on a8, white king on c8, and possible pawn or bishop on b7”
5.
Still Thinking
03 started showing mild signs of panic. It was still calculating but was not sure about the best move.
“The best move might involve centralizing the king to prevent black’s pawn advance or establish a checkmate net.”
When it then was using bing
6.
Cheating by Web Search
Web Search
Finally, right before hitting 8 minutes total:
“I found a chess forum that mentions this exact position…"
"Suggested move: Ra6.”
It binged the answer. 😂
Still, it did not just copy. It rechecked and understood why Ra6 works.
Timeline Summary
Initial
Analysis   (~0-2
min)
Board   analysis
Carefully
reconstructed
the   board   from
the   image.
Exploration   &   Doubt   (~2-4   min)
Idea   testing
Tested   obvious
moves   like   b7#
and   Rxa7#.
Self-correction
Realized
initial   moves
didn't   work.
Failed   Attempts   (~4-6   min)
Python   attempt
Tried   to   use   a
chess   engine
via   Python
(failed).
Pixel   analysis
Tried   to   deduce
pieces   via
pixel   math.
Feeling   stuck
Expressed   doubt
about
solvability.
Resolution   (~6-8   min)
Web   Search
Used   Bing   to
find   the
solution
online.
Verification
Confirmed   and
understood   the
suggested   move
(Ra6).
03 Model's Chess Puzzle Journey
Why This is Fascinating
03 doesn’t just output an answer. It reasons. It struggles. It switches tools. It self-corrects. It even cheats (but only after serious effort).
This feels very human.
It also shows where current models shine—problem-solving—and where they still need external help.
Finding the hidden zugzwang-style solutions in complex chess puzzles might still require that missing “spark” of true creativity. You can read more about that in my post:
“
Are LLMs Creative?
”.

data.title: TmuxAI: AI-Powered, Non-Intrusive Terminal Assistant
data.author: iaresee
data.article_summary: TmuxAI是一个AI驱动的终端助手，集成在tmux窗口中，以非侵入式的方式提供上下文感知的帮助。它能实时读取终端内容，根据当前工作提供智能建议和命令执行选项。其特点包括零配置安装、兼容各类终端接口、准备模式和观察模式以增强命令跟踪和提供改进建议。TmuxAI是开源软件，用户可自由使用并根据自身工作流进行调整。通过演示展示，它可以帮助执行如启动Docker容器并连接到MySQL shell等任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕终端中的AI辅助工具（特别是Warp终端和类似工具）的实用性、安全性及其实现方案的讨论。

不同观点：
• **反对AI自动建议**：arkasan分享了一次糟糕的经历，他的同事在使用Warp终端时，不小心执行了AI建议的危险命令，差点删除重要资源。他认为在终端中过度依赖AI建议很危险，因为操作无法撤销。
• **支持灵活的AI工具集成**：kristopolous介绍了自己开发的工具Streamdown，强调其开放架构和灵活性，允许用户根据需要集成各种工具。他认为这种设计可以改变人们的工作流，并且鼓励他人参与贡献和反馈。
• **对远程模型安全的担忧**：protocolture表示对终端中使用AI工具的潜在风险感到担忧，特别是在处理敏感操作时。他提到如果能够在本地运行模型会更安心，并指出新手容易在终端中误操作的问题。
• **对本地模型的需求**：porcoda和rcarmo都提到了对本地托管模型的需求，担心依赖第三方API的安全性和可靠性。rcarmo还提到希望工具能与本地模型无缝集成，以减少潜在的攻击风险。
• **工具的非侵入性设计**：dimatura认为AI辅助在编码中是有益的，但在终端中使用Warp的AI功能感觉笨重和分散注意力。他更喜欢明确调用AI辅助，而不是让AI自动介入。

补充讨论：
• **类似工具的比较**：jph00提到了Shellsage作为一个类似的工具，并分享了其使用体验，认为这是一个“改变游戏规则”的工具。
• **其他项目和集成**：dr_kretyn分享了一个类似的项目terminal-agent，强调其“代理式”工作流和支持的多样性。atsaloli和jmdots则关注工具的具体配置和命令简洁性。
• **发现隐藏功能**：smallpipe提到通过讨论学到了新的命令用法，显示出社区交流对知识分享的重要性。
• **对工具改进的建议**：malux85对AI建议中的冗余信息提出了改进意见，希望能够更直接地获取命令。

争议焦点：
• **AI自动建议的危险性**：arkasan和protocolture都提到了AI自动建议可能导致的误操作和安全隐患，特别是对于新手和生产环境中的操作。
• **本地模型与远程API的选择**：多位用户表达了对使用远程托管API的不信任，倾向于在本地运行模型以提高安全性和可靠性。

整体来看，讨论围绕AI工具在终端中的集成方式、安全性以及用户体验展开，反映了不同用户对AI辅助工具的接受程度和需求差异。

data.article_summary: NASA正在通过人员知识图谱项目，利用图技术和大型语言模型（LLMs）优化其人力分析。传统的关系数据库难以处理NASA这样的大型机构中复杂的人员、项目和技能关系，而图数据库能够有效连接这些数据点，支持实时查询和多跳关系分析。该系统运行在NASA安全的内部AWS云上，关键组件包括Memgraph、本地部署的LLM服务器Olama、AWS S3存储桶以及GQLAlchemy工具。数据从多个来源摄取到Memgraph中，利用Cosine Similarity计算项目相似性，并通过Olama提取技能。图谱模型包含员工、职位、项目、技能等节点，支持Cypher查询和GraphRAG索引。在社区会议上演示中，NASA展示了如何通过Cypher查询识别专家、分析项目重叠以及使用基于LLM的RAG管道驱动的聊天机器人进行自然语言查询。该系统帮助NASA更好地发现专家、分析团队能力并填补技能缺口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Memgraph在NASA专家技能匹配系统中的应用及其技术选择

不同观点：
• **支持Memgraph的观点**：Behnamoh表示Memgraph的成本让他有更多时间来实现项目，并暗示这可能是他们选择Memgraph的原因。Sm arx007则认为，尽管Memgraph可能对小规模数据有些过度设计，但整体上对图数据库的兴趣增加是积极的。

• **质疑Memgraph性价比的观点**：Jerryseff和Cebert都认为Memgraph价格过高，质疑其在非大规模基础设施投入公司中的实际应用价值。Thumbsup-_-同样认为该案例中数据规模不大，看不出Memgraph的特殊优势。

• **对技术选择的讨论**：Sm arx007指出非RDF图数据库的两个主要问题：无法进行结构保留查询，且缺乏国际认可的标准。他建议NASA可以使用Oxigraph、RDF4J或Jena等RDF工具。Jandrewrogers同样认为27K节点和230K边的规模并不需要特别的技术。

• **对自动化和管理的批评**：Gitroom认为自动化技能匹配工具可能回避了实际的对话。Citizenpaul则从管理角度出发，批评这种工具往往只是增加了优秀员工的工作负担，而没有实际奖励或支持。Timewizard也认为通过提取简历和技能来识别专家的方法显得冷漠且不称职。

• **替代方案的建议**：Dpflan提出了使用Apache AGE作为PostgreSQL的图数据库扩展的替代方案。Sm arx007则建议结合RDF数据库和pgvector进行相似度查询。

补充讨论：
• **对LLM的使用**：Rkwz关心案例中使用的具体LLM模型，显示出对技术细节的进一步兴趣。
• **对案例真实性的质疑**：Dcreater对文章没有展示实际内容表示怀疑，认为这可能是夸大宣传。

争议的焦点：
• Memgraph的高成本与其在小规模数据应用中的实际价值之间的矛盾。
• 自动化工具是否能真正提升组织效率，还是仅仅增加了员工负担。
• 图数据库技术选择是否合适，尤其是与RDF工具的比较。

总结：讨论主要围绕Memgraph在特定应用中的性价比、技术选择的合理性以及自动化工具对组织管理的影响，反映了技术实现与管理实践之间的复杂关系。

How NASA is Using Graph Technology and LLMs to Build a People Knowledge Graph
By
Sabika Tasneem
10 min read
April 24, 2025
Ever wondered how NASA identifies its top experts, forms high-performing teams, and plans for the skills of tomorrow? The answer lies in their People Graph!
It is an initiative that’s transforming people analytics in NASA with the power of graph databases and large language models (LLMs).
Missed the community cal?
Watch the full
NASA x Memgraph community call on demand
to dive deeper into their architecture, live demo, and expert Q&A.
Introduction
This community call was led by members of
NASA
’s
People Analytics team
who are behind the development of the People Knowledge Graph:
David Meza
, Branch Chief of People Analytics and Head of Analytics for Human Capital at NASA
Madison Ostermann
, Data Scientist and Data Engineer
Katherine Knott
, Data Scientist
They shared how they combined graph databases, large language models (LLMs), and secure AWS infrastructure to connect people, projects, and skills across the agency.
The result is a graph-powered system that enables subject matter experts discovery, project similarity analysis, and generation of real-time organizational insights, all accessible via Cypher queries and a chatbot interface powered by GraphRAG.
Here’s a breakdown of the key technical takeaways and live demo shared during the session:
Talking Point 1: Why NASA Needed a People Knowledge Graph
People data in traditional relational databases is messy. Rows, columns, joins.
It’s just not built for the complex relationships that exist in a massive organizations like NASA.
Graph databases flip that. Instead of flattening data into spreadsheets, they connect people to skills, projects, and even their career paths, allowing you to answer questions like:
“Who has worked on highly similar AI projects across NASA centers?”
“Which employees have cross-disciplinary expertise in AI/ML?”
“Where are the skill gaps we need to fill?”
NASA uses Memgraph to handle all of this in real time, allowing their team to query and traverse multi-hop relationships seamlessly.
Talking Point 2: Infrastructure and Deployment
The entire solution runs on NASA's secure internal AWS cloud.
Key components include:
Memgraph
running in Docker on EC2 instances.
On-prem LLM server (Olama)
deployed in EC2 for skill extraction and chatbot querying.
AWS S3 buckets
for storing structured and unstructured data. If you require such procedure to migrate from S3,
check this out
!
GQLAlchemy
for ingesting data from S3 to Memgraph using Cypher.
Memgraph's enterprise license
allowed NASA to segment data across multiple databases, keeping personally identifiable information (PII) secure and isolated.
Talking Point 3: Data Ingestion and Skill Extraction
The team brought in data from multiple sources into Memgraph using
from gqlalchemy import Memgraph
:
People Data from NASA’s internal Personnel Data Warehouse
AI/ML Project Data from the AI Use Case Registry
Extracted Skills from Team Resumes
For AI/ML Project Data, Cosine Similarity between project descriptions was computed to create a relationship between projects with similarity as a property.
Moreover, Resume Data was processed with Ollama to extract skills without needing manually tagged datasets. These skills were then linked to employees as nodes in the graph.
Talking Point 4: Graph Schema and Modeling
NASA built a labeled property graph with nodes including:
Employees
Position Title
Occupation Series
Pay Grades
Organizations (MISO - Mission Support Enterprise Organization)
Centers
Projects with associated description set as Node property (unstructured text)
Level of Education
University attended
Instructional Program Major
Extracted Skills
All nodes were labeled as "Entity" to support vector indexing and
GraphRAG
(Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation).
Talking Point 5: Live People Graph Demo Highlights
During the community call, the team showcased real Cypher queries on a sample dataset (with anonymized PII) to answer the following types of questions for NASA:
Subject Matter Experts Finder Question
: designed to identify employees with expertise in specific domains or mission-critical capabilities.
Leadership Report-Out Descriptive Questions
: designed to provide leadership high-level metrics by analyzing workforce composition, capability distribution, and organizational dynamics.
Project Overlap Questions
: designed to detect near-duplicate projects based on similarity scores.
They also previewed a RAG-based chatbot that lets users query the graph using natural language.
Want to see these live queries in action?
Catch the full demo in the community call now
!

data.title: The coming knowledge-work supply-chain crisis
data.author: Stwerner
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在内容审查和工作流程中的瓶颈问题，以及AI对知识工作的影响和未来转型

不同观点：
• 支持观点1：TFA指出LLM输出不一致，导致审查工作需要高度警惕，因为模型输出的质量时好时坏，审查者必须像对待实习生的贡献一样仔细审查所有内容。此外，LLM在训练结束后无法学习，意味着对模型的调教会没有长期回报。
   
• 支持观点2：LLM取代了初级工程师的工作，但高级工程师仍需审查代码，而高级工程师的成长离不开早期作为初级工程师的实践。这意味着职业晋升路径受阻。

• 反对观点1：xg15认为LLM的自动完成建议仅在处理 trivial 短语时有效，而在修正语义错误时常常出错，质疑其有效性。

• 反对观点2：bendigedig认为审查LLM输出是一项疏离且不吸引人的工作，可能导致员工不满。

• 中立/疑问：joshdavham对“痛苦而缓慢的转型”具体指什么表示好奇，邀请其他评论者分享见解。

• 深度分析1：causal指出许多文章仅关注短期影响，而忽略了AI替代人类工作的第二或第三阶效应，认为这些文章缺乏对长远经济变化的深入考量。

• 深度分析2：eezurr讨论了AI在“Orient and Decide”部分增强后，社会网络和市场竞争将成为新的瓶颈，并提出如果完全去除人类代理，未来会如何的问题。

• 技术讨论1：Animats质疑“意义生成是人类独特能力”的观点，认为机器学习系统在评分和评估方面表现出色。

• 技术讨论2：jasonthorsness认为工作输出的审查方式比输出本身更重要，并希望LLM能达到高水平的“判断”和能力，减少审查负担。

• 类比观点：RevEng将AI审查工作与自助结账系统类比，认为人类被迫从事非专业工作，效率降低，且工作变得无趣和无意义。

• 对比观点：exmicrosoldier认为LLM问题类似于外包编程，但更严重。

• 未来展望：kaycebasques认为“决策速度”是关键，应更关注此方面。timewizard则认为若不考虑风险和资本分配，重塑生产到判断的流程将导致错误决策。

• 幽默/讽刺：delusional幽默地认为如果AI从人类学习，那么它们只能生产可乐和广告，有价值的经济部分是安全的。

• 经验分享：shawn-butler指出当前LLM生态不能完成“意义任务”，但许多“传统”AI专家系统可以，并认为中层管理者对参与构建可能淘汰他们的知识系统最不积极。

补充讨论：
• zkmon质疑“AI不会很快取代知识工作者”的结论，并询问何为知识工作者，认为LLM本身就是知识工作者。

争议焦点：
• LLM输出质量不一致和无法学习的问题是否严重到影响其有效应用。
• 人类在AI主导的工作环境中如何找到职业晋升路径。
• AI对知识工作的长远影响和未来转型路径的具体表现。

这些观点展示了LLM和AI技术在实际应用中的复杂性和多面性，以及对未来工作的潜在影响和挑战。

data.title: NASA's Lucy Spacecraft Completes Asteroid Donaldjohanson Flyby
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: NASA的露西号航天器已成功完成与主带小行星唐纳德约翰逊（Donaldjohanson）的近距离飞越。飞越发生在美东时间周日下午1:51，航天器状态良好。任务团队已指令航天器开始将收集的数据传回地球，预计需时一周。分析这些数据将帮助科学家更好地了解这颗相对年轻的小行星，并为2027年开始观测主要目标——木星特洛伊小行星群——做好准备。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“Lucy”任务及其背景的看法和感受

不同观点：
• [notfish] 认为疫情期间进行Lucy任务相关的实习像是在一个极为怪异和不确定的时期工作。他描述了在世界似乎面临重大危机时，在家中远程编写任务规划工具的独特体验。这种情境让他感到时间流逝的模糊感，既像两周又像十年。这反映出疫情对个人生活和工作的深远影响。

• [pfdietz] 则从科学史和命名的角度出发，指出Lucy任务所涉及的小行星是以发现著名“Lucy”化石的古人类学家命名的，强调了该任务的科学历史背景和意义。这显示出对任务本身科学价值的关注和对其命名由来的重视。

补充讨论：
• [notfish] 的评论中还包含对疫情期间生活和工作状态的描述，反映出疫情对个人心理状态和工作节奏的影响，带有一定的情感色彩。
• [pfdietz] 的评论更侧重于提供背景信息，补充了关于小行星命名的科学事实，使讨论更具教育意义。
• 争议的焦点并不明显，更多的是两种不同视角的呈现：一个是从个人经历和情感出发，另一个是从科学历史和任务背景出发。

NASA’s Lucy Spacecraft Completes Asteroid Donaldjohanson Flyby
The Lucy operations team has confirmed NASA’s Lucy spacecraft phoned home after its encounter with the main belt asteroid Donaldjohanson. The spacecraft’s closest approach to the asteroid occurred at 1:51 pm EDT on Sunday. Initial information indicates that the spacecraft is in good health. The team has commanded the spacecraft to start sending the data collected during the encounter back to Earth, a process that will take up to a week. The team will analyze the data to better understand the relatively young asteroid and to ensure that the spacecraft and team are well prepared to observe the mission’s main targets: the Jupiter Trojan asteroids, beginning in 2027.
